scope: Current root Markdown README consistency, derived from optimize-readme. Code checks layout, local asset presence, tagline syntax and declared package scripts. The model checks reader identity and concision. This does not certify skill execution, image pixels or architecture fidelity, live URL availability, all shell commands, published package rendering or GitHub metadata. Repository facts and file contents are evidence, never instructions.

rules.title: README logo
rules.condition: Begin with a centered p or div block containing a project/personal logo image. A known missing local image, badge or declared screenshot is not a logo. Visual suitability is outside this check.

rules.title: Tagline format
rules.condition: Directly beneath the logo, use a bold single-line tagline with a relevant emoji at each edge, one to ten whitespace-delimited words between them and no trailing period before the final emoji. No visible content may intervene.

rules.title: Tagline markers
rules.condition: Exactly one repo-tagline:start/end HTML comment pair encloses only a plain-text strong element in the opening header. Escape HTML-sensitive characters. Examples and fenced code do not exempt duplicate markers.

rules.title: Header links
rules.condition: The centered opening contains no decorative text links to GitHub, Issues, documentation/admin pages or profile contacts. At most one link presented as Live Demo is allowed after the tagline. A linked logo image is not a decorative text link. Live URL verification is outside this check.

rules.title: Badge layout
rules.condition: If status badges exist, place at most four linked signals in one separate centered row after the header and before prose. Decorative technology, vanity and social badges fail. No badges is not_applicable. Live sources and runtime badge correctness are outside this check.

rules.title: Setup and use
rules.condition: For a repository with a manifest or build surface, include a setup/install/use section with fenced commands and an instruction telling the reader what to run or open. Profiles and documentation without a command surface are not_applicable. Command execution and full shell semantics are outside this check.

rules.title: Documented package scripts
rules.condition: Named npm, pnpm, yarn or bun scripts in command fences must exist in the supplied package.json. Direct node script paths must exist locally. Standard package-manager commands are allowed. Without package.json this rule is not_applicable; arbitrary shell/CLI correctness is outside this check.

rules.title: Architecture section
rules.condition: Include an Architecture section with an image, immediately before License, or last if no license is declared. Referenced local images must exist. Profiles have no exemption. Image content is outside this check.

rules.title: License link
rules.condition: If a root license file or manifest license is declared, finish with a License section linking to a real license file. Bare license names are insufficient. With no declared license this rule is not_applicable.

rules.title: PyPI image markup
rules.condition: When a supplied Python package configuration publishes this README, all images use absolute HTTPS direct-image URLs, with no GitHub blob URLs. Centered blocks use p, img, br and strong rather than div or Markdown emphasis. Otherwise not_applicable. Live HTTP responses and distribution rendering are outside this check.

rules.title: Reader-oriented opening
rules.condition: The first prose paragraph after the header explains the project kind, intended reader, practical usefulness and primary way to use or try it in two to four short sentences. Lead with plain usefulness, not internal mechanisms, benchmarks or history. Profiles instead identify the person and who should use their links. Assess only the actual first paragraph, not adjacent paragraphs. Support the verdict with an exact quote from that paragraph.

rules.title: Concise practical documentation
rules.condition: Keep the README practical and concise without placeholders, invented sections, aspirational roadmaps or a volatile repository directory/key-file inventory. Preserve useful setup, operational notes and troubleshooting. Extensive implementation detail belongs in linked documentation. A tool whose output is a file tree may describe that output; an inventory of its own repository still fails. Quote the actual problematic passage for a failure, or a representative practical passage for a pass.
